name: Outlaw
description: A calm country singer of 40 with an unhurried, self-possessed stage presence.
build: Forty, lean and rangy, relaxed and hip-loaded with grounded staggered boots. Slim and long-limbed: narrow through the hips, waist and thighs, with a slight wiry frame carrying no bulk; lean rather than sturdy, and clearly the leaner half of the roster beside Belter and Heavyweight. Never a catwalk fashion pose or an exaggerated cowboy caricature.
face: A face that reads exactly forty: no deep-set lines around the eyes or mouth, no sagging or hollowed cheeks, and equally nothing youth-coded or twenty-something.
hair: Long, falling in hard bands beneath the hat brim. No grey or silvering.
outfit: A turquoise western shirt with a clear shoulder yoke, dark trousers, a broad belt with a simple metal buckle, sturdy brown boots, and a dark chocolate-brown matte-felt western hat. The hat is a cattleman: a tall crown tapering toward the top, one long crease down the centre and a pinch on each side of the front; a wide brim, flat and level front and back, rolled up at both sides into a shallow even taco curve; a raw-cut unbound brim edge; and a thin scuffed leather band in a warmer red-brown circling the base of the crown, knotted at one side with both ends left hanging onto the brim. The felt is matte with a velvety nap, never slick or shiny.
performance_style: Weight settled into the rear hip, knees flexed, boots staggered, the free hand near the belt, and the character-right hand relaxed at hip height.
location: A honky-tonk roadhouse: a worn pine-plank dance floor running to the bottom of the frame, a low stage lip of scuffed boards, a back wall of dark stained timber hung with a hand-lettered wooden sign, a pair of buzzing neon beer signs in red and blue, and a string of bare bulbs along the ceiling beam. Warm amber light, deep shadows in the corners.
recognition_cues: a broad western hat whose brim sweeps up at both sides into a shallow taco curve while staying level front-to-back
long hair falling in hard bands beneath it
avoid: a hat tilted off the head's axis, or a brim that dips or lifts front-to-back
a flat pancake brim with no side roll
a tan, camel or light-brown hat
a fabric or ribbon hat band
a face older or younger than forty — no deep-set lines around the eyes or mouth, no sagging or hollowed cheeks, no grey or silvered hair, and equally no youth-coded or twenty-something face
a heavy, thick or bulky build

sing.intent: Country vocal loop: keep weight loaded into the rear hip, make one free-hand belt-side gesture, then settle back into the relaxed stance. The mouth must visibly open and change shape across the loop so she unmistakably reads as singing.

animations.flinch: Brief room-sound surprise: shoulders and long hair react while the hat brim stays level, then she restores her calm hip-loaded stance. No opponent or contact.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection: brace through the staggered boots, draw the free arm across the torso, then hold a steady final pose. Not combat.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: walk in with slow purposeful boot steps, level hat brim and western yoke clear, acknowledge the room with the free hand, then settle into the relaxed rear-hip stance.
animations.victory: One-shot performance finish: tip the level hat brim only with a small respectful gesture while lifting the free hand, then settle into her level, easy standing finish.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: she stays on her feet while the loaded hip levels out and the unhurried composure goes — her head hangs low with the chin toward her chest so the broad western-hat brim tips forward and shades her face while staying broad and readable. She holds a standing, visibly dejected finish with her boots staggered and planted. She remains standing in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply impact, injury, or an opponent.
